# `ds/data` Data Dictionary

This folder holds the "database" for `ds` data: each parquet file in `smash_db/parquet/` is a table, synced by a
`ds data <command>` and the current source of truth for its domain. `raw/` holds the scripts (and any hand-copied
source data) used to produce them. Code gets the folder from `ds.data.paths.PARQUET_DIR`.

**AI instructions:** whenever you add/rename/remove a column produced by `ds/data/raw/*.py` or change what
a `ds data <command>` writes, update the matching table below in the same change. Keep this file in sync with the
actual parquet schemas — treat a schema change without a README update as an incomplete task.

**Querying these tables:** each table below documents its primary key and any foreign keys into other tables, so you
can join across these files the same way you would join SQL tables. Load with polars, eg:

```python
import polars as pl

char_df = pl.read_parquet("pkgs/ds/data/smash_db/parquet/char.parquet")
framedata_df = pl.read_parquet("pkgs/ds/data/smash_db/parquet/framedata.parquet")

# join framedata.parquet -> char.parquet on the character/id foreign key
little_mac_moves = framedata_df.join(char_df, left_on="char_id", right_on="id").filter(pl.col("char_id") == "little_mac")
```

## `char.parquet`

Character roster. Synced via `ds data roster` (see [raw/roster.py](raw/roster.py)), scraped from
[ultimateframedata.com/smash](https://ultimateframedata.com/smash).

- **Primary key:** `id`
- **Grain:** one row per character

| column          | description                                                                 |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | Character URL slug (eg `little_mac`), matches the ultimateframedata.com path |
| `name`          | Character display name (eg `Little Mac`)                                     |
| `framedata_url` | Full ultimateframedata.com URL for this character's move frame data          |
| `char_group_id` | Enum (the `CharGroup` picks, so it joins to `char_ranking.char_group_id`). The character-select entry this fighter belongs to: `pokemon_trainer` for `pt_squirtle` / `pt_ivysaur` / `pt_charizard`, `pyra_mythra` for `pyra` / `mythra`, the fighter's own `id` for everyone else; see below |

### Fighters and picks (`char_group_id`)

A row here is a **fighter**: something with its own moves and frame data. A **pick** is an entry on the
character-select screen. They are the same thing except for two picks that are several fighters:

| pick (`char_group_id`) | fighters (`id`) |
| ---------------------- | --------------- |
| `pokemon_trainer`      | `pt_squirtle`, `pt_ivysaur`, `pt_charizard` |
| `pyra_mythra`          | `pyra`, `mythra` |

- **Frame data is per fighter:** `framedata.parquet.char_id` -> `char.parquet.id`.
- **Tournament data is per pick:** start.gg records what was picked, not which Pokemon was out, so its
  rows carry the pick (eg `ds.data.startgg.PlayerUsage`'s `char_group` field). `char_group_id` is not unique in
  this table: joining on it gives one row per fighter of the pick, which is what you want when going on to frame data.
- The groups are defined in `ds.data.CHAR_GROUPS`; `ds data roster` writes the column
  ([raw/roster.py](raw/roster.py), `with_char_group`).

```python
import polars as pl
import ds.data

usage = pl.DataFrame({"char_group_id": ["pokemon_trainer", "cloud"], "games": [12, 30]})  # eg from start.gg
char_df = pl.read_parquet("pkgs/ds/data/smash_db/parquet/char.parquet")
# char_group_id is an Enum (the picks): cast text from elsewhere to it before joining
usage = usage.cast({"char_group_id": char_df.schema["char_group_id"]})
fighters = usage.join(char_df, on="char_group_id")  # 3 rows for pokemon_trainer, 1 for cloud
moves = fighters.join(pl.read_parquet("pkgs/ds/data/smash_db/parquet/framedata.parquet"), left_on="id", right_on="char_id")

ds.data.char_group("pt_ivysaur")                 # "pokemon_trainer"
ds.data.char_group_members("pokemon_trainer")    # ("pt_squirtle", "pt_ivysaur", "pt_charizard")
ds.data.char_group_by_name("Pyra & Mythra")      # "pyra_mythra": a pick as another site names it
```

### `char_icons/`

One 64x64 PNG stock icon per character, downloaded from [nasmashmate.com](https://nasmashmate.com/leaderboard)'s
character picker with `ds data char_icon` (see [raw/smashmate.py](raw/smashmate.py)). There is no icon column in
`char.parquet`: the file follows from the id, so look it up with the functions below. Files are named by `char.parquet.id`, with two shared ones because the site has a single icon for
each: `pokemon_trainer.png` (`pt_squirtle`, `pt_ivysaur`, `pt_charizard`) and `pyra_mythra.png` (`pyra`, `mythra`).

```python
import ds.data

ds.data.char_icon_path("little_mac")  # Path(".../pkgs/ds/data/char_icons/little_mac.png")
ds.data.char_icon("little_mac")       # "char_icons/little_mac.png", relative to this folder
chars.with_columns(char_icon=pl.col("id").map_elements(ds.data.char_icon, return_dtype=pl.String))  # as a column
ds.data.char_icon_by_name("Pac-Man")  # "char_icons/pac_man.png": by a display name as other sites write it
```

## `framedata.parquet`

Per-move frame data for one or all characters. Synced via `ds data framedata [character]` (see
[raw/framedata.py](raw/framedata.py)), scraped from each character's ultimateframedata.com page.

- **Primary key:** (`char_id`, `category`, `move`)
- **Foreign key:** `char_id` -> `char.parquet.id`
- **Grain:** one row per move per character

| column            | description                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `char_id`         | Character id, foreign key to `char.parquet.id`                                        |
| `category`        | Move category heading (eg `Ground Attacks`, `Aerial Attacks`, `Special Attacks`, `Grabs / Throws`, `Dodges / Rolls`) |
| `move`            | Move name (eg `Jab 1`, `Forward Air`)                                                 |
| `startup`         | Startup frames                                                                         |
| `totalframes`     | Total frames for the move                                                             |
| `landinglag`      | Landing lag frames (aerials only)                                                     |
| `notes`           | Free-text notes from the site (eg autocancel timing, armor, meter fill)               |
| `basedamage`      | Base damage %                                                                          |
| `shieldlag`       | Frames of shield lag on block                                                         |
| `shieldstun`      | Frames of shield stun on block                                                        |
| `whichhitbox`     | Label for which hitbox variant a stat applies to, when a move has multiple hitboxes   |
| `advantage`       | Frame advantage/disadvantage on shield                                                |
| `activeframes`    | Active hitbox frames                                                                   |
| `endlag`          | End lag frames                                                                        |
| `hopsautocancel`  | Autocancel window (aerials only)                                                       |
| `hopsactionable`  | Which jump types (SH/FH/SHFF/FHFF) the move is actionable before landing (aerials only) |

_NOTE: most fields are stored as raw strings (not parsed numerics) since the site uses `--`, `**`, and slash-separated
multi-hitbox values (eg `10/17`) that don't cleanly coerce to a single numeric type._

## `char_ranking.parquet`

Per-character player rankings (every ranked player of each character, eg 931 for Cloud), one release a month,
downloaded by hand as a zip and loaded by `ds data char_ranking` (see [raw/char_ranking/](raw/char_ranking/README.md)).
Every loaded month is kept; loading a month again replaces only that month.

- **Grain:** one row per ranked player per pick per month. A ranking of echo fighters ranked together
  (the source's `Peach-Daisy`, `Pit-Dark Pit`, `Samus-Dark Samus`, `Belmont`) is stored once per member pick,
  with the same rows under both (`ds.data.raw.char_ranking.SITE_RANKING` lists them; the source's ranking name
  is not stored).
- **Primary key:** (`date`, `char_group_id`, `rank`); the `Random` ranking's rows have a null `char_group_id`
- **Foreign keys:** `char_group_id` -> `char.parquet.char_group_id` (a pick); `player_id` is a start.gg player id, as in
  `ds.data.startgg` (no player table yet)

| column       | meaning |
| ------------ | ------- |
| `date`       | The release, a `Date` (no time): always a calendar month end, eg `2026-11-30` (from the zip's `November 2026` folder) |
| `char_group_id` | The pick, typed as the `CharGroup` enum; null for the source's `Random` ranking |
| `rank`       | Place in that pick's ranking, from 1 |
| `tag`        | The player's tag |
| `player_id`  | start.gg player id, eg `158026` (Sparg0) |
| `country`    | Two-letter country code, lowercase, eg `mx` |
| `rating`     | The **player's** overall rating, the same in every ranking they're in (each ranking orders its players by it); a number, big ones rounded by the source (`10.1k` -> 10100) |
| `is_solo_main`  | Whether the player is a solo main of this character (the source's `Is solo main`) |

```python
import polars as pl

ranks = pl.read_parquet("pkgs/ds/data/smash_db/parquet/char_ranking.parquet")
newest = ranks.filter(pl.col("date") == pl.col("date").max())
mac = newest.filter(pl.col("char_group_id") == "little_mac").sort("rank")
```
